summary: Every course needs a C or better, and every course except up to 10 Philosophy units in the French and Philosophy subplan must be letter graded. You take three 100- or 200-level courses taught in French (or FRENLANG 124) for 12 units, a course on a period before 1800, a WIM course, the 3-unit FRENCH 199 capstone and the Oral Proficiency Interview, with FRENCH electives and up to three French language courses at or above FRENLANG 21C (12 units) making up 60 units; at most 12 units of independent study count. The optional French and Philosophy subplan raises the total to 66 units and adds three FRENCH courses numbered 140 or above, FRENCH 181, PHIL 80, a 170-series and a 180-series course, two history of philosophy courses, two approved electives and its own capstone. Courses from other departments, Bing Overseas Paris, ESF, SLE and Digital Humanities count with the Director of Undergraduate Studies' approval and are moved in by hand, as are transfer units (at most 12); whether a course is taught in French or covers the pre-1800 period is checked by hand. Honors adds 9 units of DLCL 189H, the thesis and the colloquium.

program.why: Grading: "All courses applied to the major must be taken for a letter grade and passed with at least a C." GPA: "A grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or better must be achieved in each course." The letter grade is set on each rule rather than program-wide, because the French and Philosophy subplan lets up to 10 Philosophy units be CR/NC or S/NC.

children.name: 5,000-word Topic Paper
children.desc:
The student will write a 5,000-word paper on a topic of their choosing, serving as the culmination of their work in the field.
To write the paper, students must enroll in a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member (or affiliate) in the Philosophy and Literature Focal Group. The paper must involve philosophy and literature, and the faculty member must approve the topic by the add/drop deadline.
